newsitem.title: USA: Minntech sees Q2 below expectations.
newsitem.headline: Minntech sees Q2 below expectations.

text.p: Minntech Corp said it expects its second quarter results to fall below market expectations.
"Revenues were below expectations for the second quarter," said chairman and chief executive Louis Cosentino.

On June 27, Minntech advised customers to stop using its Biocor blood oxygenator as a component in heart-lung bypass circuits for heart surgery. The Biocor had experienced some problems, but Minntech withdrew the advisory on July 18 and said the product was safe to use under amended instructions.

Second-quarter "results were impacted by the Biocor oxygenator advisory early in the quarter and by Minntech's inability to obtain (U.S. Food and Drug Administration) approval for the U.S. introduction of the Biocor oxygenator. We have submitted additional information to FDA this week for their review," Cosentino said.
The company's second quarter ended September 30.

"Since canceling the advisory ... we are seeing positive results with the Biocor oxygenator in Europe. Earlier this week, Minntech received regulatory approval for the Biocor in Japan. However, this international growth is insufficient to offset the decrease in revenues the company is experiencing as a result of the scheduled reduction of shipments of the HF5000 oxygenator to C.R. Bard (Inc)," Cosentino said.
He added, "Although our cardiosurgery business has been affected by these setbacks with the Biocor, we are achieving steady growth in our dialysis supplies and reprocessing businesses."
Minntech makes products for use in dialysis, reprocessing and sterilants, cardiosurgery, and water purification.
Shares in the company closed up 1/4 at 13-1/2 on Thursday.
